liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **He's Gone** (2 reviews): He's Gone ends with a nice little jam; Nice thrum at the end of He's Gone [21][22]
- **Iko Iko** (1 review): Iko Iko was fairly rare at that time [20]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Reviewer quotes lyrics about crawling if unable to dance, noting Garcia goes off [14]
- **Brown Eyed Women** (1 review): Reviewer calls this their favorite version ever [11]
- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): Garcia's vocals sound strained here, though he remembers the words [11]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): China Cat into Rider is called nice, with superb playing and song choices after Drums/Space [19]
- **China Doll** (1 review): A pretty China Doll in 1984, when it appeared in about one in five shows [18]
- **I Need A Miracle** (1 review): The transition from Miracle into Bertha sounds crunchy [15]

## The recordings

- **gd84-07-01.aud.willy.14683.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 20 songs; 135 min; rated 2.5/5 by 4 [1]. Said about its sound: Audience source is clear, with distinct instrument representation; Reviewer prefers soundboards because the barn-like venue is unkind to audience tapes [12][14]
- **gd1984-07-01.150292.beyerm88.holbrook.flac2448**: source not stated; 20 songs; 135 min [2]
- **gd1984-07-01.nak100.reutelhuber.25810.sbefail.shnf**: source not stated; 19 songs; 137 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [7]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is good for an outdoor 1984 show [16]
- **gd1984-07-01.nak300-set2.wise.andrewf.76620.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 11 songs; 77 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [10]. Said about its sound: Keyboards sound thick on the set-two recording [15]

## Around the show

- Reviewer's first tour; Pine Knob was about 15 minutes from their childhood home, and it was their 18th birthday [20]
- Reviewer finds the second set short but acceptable and the first set very good [16]
- China Doll frequency in 1984 was exceeded only by 1973 at 23% and 1974 at 30% [18]
- Second set is a bit mellower than the Saturday night Indianapolis show [19]
- The end of set two is described as rollicking [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd84-07-01.aud.willy.14683.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD>MC>??>DAT>CDR [1]. Also: Audience recording transferred through microphone, unknown steps, DAT and CDR; came via Paul B and seeded to etree by Willy [1]
- **gd1984-07-01.150292.beyerm88.holbrook.flac2448**: taped by Executive Crew - Tom Pinney, Kyle Holbrook; transferred by Kyle Holbrook; source: MAUD CA: Beyer M88's XY > Sony TCD5M|Sony UCX-S90 x2 no NR Location: 100 feet from stage DFC 6 feet up [2]. Also: Baby Blue tape stopped between tracks to save tape; the tape flip cut the ending, missing about three seconds [2]
- **gd1984-07-01.nak100.reutelhuber.25810.sbefail.shnf**: taped by Bill Reutelhuber; source: Nak CM100 shotgun mics > Sony TCD5M (lead deck) > Dolby B noise reduction > MAC (Maxell MX 90 Metal tape) [7]
- **gd1984-07-01.nak300-set2.wise.andrewf.76620.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Ted Carpenter; transferred by Jim Wise and Andrew F.; source: FOB, Nakamichi CM-300's with CP-4 shotgun capsules > [10]. Also: First set and encore tape is lost; set-two tape flip during Drums cuts at 08:07.806, and Soundforge cleaned the pauses [10]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Steve Schneider Grateful Dead: [1984-07-01 Pine Knob Music Theater, Clarkston, MI, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1984-07-01-pine-knob-music-theater-clarkston-mi-usa/) [24]
- Fan art by Steve Schneider Grateful Dead: [1984-07-01 Pine Knob Music Theater, Clarkston, MI, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1984-07-01-pine-knob-music-theater-clarkston-mi-usa/) [25]
